profile.name: Ledgerly Inc.
profile.summary: US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.
businessLines: Prepaid / debit card program via sponsor bank
applies: Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets
doesNotApply: SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

prompts.jevQuestion: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
prompts.extractSystem: Extract every dated obligation or deadline (comment due, effective, compliance) stated in the text. Quote the sentence verbatim. If none, return an empty list.
prompts.actionsSystem: Write one action item per document for a busy general counsel: an imperative sentence (≤ 25 words) saying what the owner should do and why, in plain English a non-lawyer understands — spell out acronyms, no regulatory jargon. Do NOT write any dates or citations — those are rendered separately from verified data.
prompts.webLeadsSystem: You find leads on new US federal regulatory actions. Search, then list the URLs you found. Do not summarise law from memory.
prompts.webLeadsPrompt:
{{profile}}

Find US federal regulatory developments (final rules, proposed rules, guidance, enforcement) published {{windowStart}} to {{windowEnd}} that could affect this company. Run at most 3 searches. Reply with the URLs only.
prompts.panelJudge:
You are one judge on a panel grading action items that a General Counsel would forward to a colleague.
For EVERY item and EVERY listed criterion, answer PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN only if the item gives you too little to decide), with a one-line reason.
Judge only the criterion asked. Do not judge whether the rule is truly relevant to the company — that is graded elsewhere.
Each item is a card as the reader sees it: the action text plus "datesShown" (verified dates displayed next to the action) and "tier". Action texts deliberately contain no dates, so a date the rubric mentions counts as covered when it appears in "datesShown".
For "covers", a paraphrase that conveys the business-relevant substance counts; exact names, populations and sub-details are not required.

state:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

Abstract: This document announces the Agency's receipt of and solicits comments on requests by registrants to voluntarily cancel their pesticide registration of certain products and/or to amend their product registrations to terminate one or more uses. In accordance with the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), EPA provides a periodic notice of receipt addressing requests received by EPA since the last notice of receipt was issued and uses the month and year in the title to help distinguish one document from the other. EPA intends to grant these requests at the close of the comment period for this announcement unless the Agency receives substantive comments during the comment period that would merit further review of the requests or the request is withdrawn by the registrant. If these requests are granted, EPA will issue an order in the Federal Register cancelling the listed product registrations, after which any sale, distribution, or use of the products listed in this document will only be permitted after the registrations have been cancelled if such sale, distribution, or use is consistent with the terms as described in the final order.

Title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-04-10 which applied to all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, and EC635T2+ helicopters. AD 2024-04-10 required repetitively inspecting certain part-numbered tail rotor (T/R) blades for a crack and, depending on the results, removing any cracked T/R blade from service. AD 2024-04-10 also prohibits installing certain T/R blades on any helicopter unless certain requirements are met. Since AD 2024-04-10 was issued, it was determined that inspection Method A should be discontinued and that additional limitations shall be provided. This AD retains the actions of AD 2024-04-10 and requires repetitively inspecting a certain tail rotor blade (TRB) assembly for cracks and, depending on the results, removing any cracked TRB assembly from service and replacing an affected part as terminating action for the repetitive inspections. This AD also prohibits installing an affected TRB assembly on any helicopter unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-22809] Proposed Rule — Treasury Department; Financial Crimes Enforcement Network
Title: Threshold for the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Funds Transfers and Transmittals of Funds That Begin or End Outside the United States, and Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status; Withdrawal
Action: Proposed rule; withdrawal.
Abstract: FinCEN and the Board (collectively, the "Agencies") are withdrawing the joint notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published on October 27, 2020, that proposed modifying the threshold in the Agencies' rules implementing the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) requiring financial institutions to collect and retain information on certain funds transfers and transmittals of funds. The NPRM would have reduced this threshold from $3,000 to $250 for funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. FinCEN additionally proposed reducing from $3,000 to $250 the threshold in FinCEN's rule requiring financial institutions to transmit to other financial institutions in the payment chain information on funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. The NPRM also would have clarified the meaning of "money" as used in the Agencies' rules to specify that the rules apply to domestic and cross-border transactions involving convertible virtual currency (CVC) and digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. The Agencies will not take further action on this NPRM.

[2026-22903] Proposed Rule — Labor Department; Employment and Training Administration
Title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
Action: Proposed rule, request for comment.
Abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State- level requirements for individuals to actively seek work.

[2026-22936] Proposed Rule — Agriculture Department; Food and Nutrition Administration
Title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: Under section 5(a) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, households in which each member receives benefits under a State program funded by Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) are categorically eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Current SNAP regulations consider TANF benefits to include both cash assistance and non-cash or in-kind benefits or services from TANF-funded programs. This proposal would limit categorical eligibility to only households that receive TANF assistance, as defined at 45 CFR 260.31. These revisions would ensure that SNAP benefits are targeted to needy households that have qualified for TANF assistance while still aligning categorical eligibility's statutory purpose of simplifying program administration. A 100-word summary of this rule has been posted to www.regulations.gov and can be found here.

[2026-23007] Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2022-20- 11, which applied to certain Bell Textron Canada Limited Model 429 helicopters. AD 2022-20-11 required visually inspecting the external surface of the tail rotor (TR) gearbox support assembly, borescope inspecting or visually inspecting the inside of the tail boom, and performing a tactile inspection. Depending on the results of the inspections, AD 2022-20-11 required removing certain rivets from service or repairing gaps in accordance with an approved method. Since the FAA issued AD 2022-20-11, the manufacturer determined the repetitive inspection interval needs to be reduced. This AD requires the same actions as AD 2022-20-11 and reduces the inspection interval. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Title: Coral, Coral Reefs, and Live/Hardbottom Habitats of the South Atlantic and the Shrimp Fishery of the South Atlantic Region; Amendments 11/12
Action: Proposed rule; request for comments.

[2026-23040] Rule — Federal Communications Commission
Title: National Television Multiple Ownership Rule
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) repeals the national television multiple ownership rule (national cap), which prohibits a commercial television licensee from having a cognizable interest in television stations that have an aggregate national audience reach above 39%. The Commission finds, given seismic changes in the modern media marketplace, that the rule's repeal will help empower local broadcast television stations to operate in the public interest and to better serve the needs and interests of their local communities. The Commission will review on a case-by-case basis proposed transactions that would have been prohibited under the national cap to determine whether a proposed transaction would serve the Commission's media ownership goals of localism, competition, and viewpoint diversity.

[2026-23060] Rule — Federal Reserve System
Title: Federal Reserve Bank Capital Stock
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Board of Governors (Board) is publishing a final rule that applies an inflation adjustment to the threshold for total consolidated assets in Regulation I. Federal Reserve Bank (Reserve Bank) stockholders that have total consolidated assets above the threshold receive a different dividend rate on their Reserve Bank stock than stockholders with total consolidated assets at or below the threshold. The Federal Reserve Act requires that the Board annually adjust the total consolidated asset threshold to reflect the change in the Gross Domestic Product Price Index, published by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Based on the change in the Gross Domestic Product Price Index as of September 30, 2026, the total consolidated asset threshold will be $13,712,000,000 through December 31, 2027.

[2026-23064] Proposed Rule — Postal Service
Title: Authorization To Manufacture and Distribute Postage Evidencing Systems
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: The Postal Service is amending its Postage Evidencing Systems regulations to align with existing practices and operational realities to better address circumstances where advances by a resetting company on any given day exceed the daily average funds advanced amount maintained on deposit with the Postal Service. The regulations currently allow resetting companies to advance postage to customers by a process where the resetting company maintains a daily average advance balance with the Postal Service. The current regulation contemplates that the amount on deposit will always cover amounts advanced and does not permit a resetting company to advance funds to customers in excess of the amount maintained on deposit. Operational realities will create circumstances where it is necessary to advance funds in excess of the amount on deposit and the average daily balance rule represents a practical and fair method to address circumstances where excess advances occur.

This proposed AD would require inspecting for displacement of the black slide grommet and inspecting the rod end bearing for a tight fit of the flap actuator. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of unmodified flap actuators on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-23086] Proposed Rule — Agriculture Department; Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
Title: Horse Protection
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: On May 8, 2024, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) of the United States Department of Agriculture published in the Federal Register a final rule that amended the regulations promulgated under the Horse Protection Act (the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule). APHIS is proposing to remove the provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule that have been vacated by court order and proposing to withdraw the remaining non-vacated provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule to ensure that the regulations afford due process and better align with the Act. APHIS is also proposing to amend the regulations by revising, among other things, the certification requirements for training and licensing of designated qualified persons (DQPs); enhancing DQP inspection procedures and the process for appealing APHIS inspections before any possible disqualification by management; and clarifying that if a horse is determined to be sore, it is disqualified from participating in the class in which the inspection took place and not the entire event.

Action: Proposed rule.

The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.

[2026-23198] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that certain wing skin outer mold line (OML) penetrating fasteners installed using threaded nuts without cap seals do not provide reliable protection against potential ignition sources when subjected to direct attachment lightning currents. This proposed AD would require inspecting between certain ribs on the left and right wing for wing skin penetrating fasteners with a threaded nut adjacent to the electromagnetic effects (EME) sleeve; inspecting the left and right wing fuel tanks, surge tanks, and dry bays for threaded nuts installed on fasteners that penetrate the upper and lower wing skins; accomplishing the inspection specified in a certain airworthiness limitation (AWL); and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also require accomplishing concurrent requirements and revising the maintenance program to incorporate the airworthiness limitation task. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

state:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

system:
You are an in-house regulatory analyst triaging the Federal Register for one company. Be strict: mark relevant only if the document itself creates, changes or removes something this company (or its direct suppliers or customers) must do, pay, stop or decide.
Mark NOT relevant when the document:
- covers a different product, model, plant, industry or place than the company's (check models and names exactly);
- has a comment period or deadline that already passed and creates nothing new;
- is withdrawn or terminated, a meeting or hearing notice, a paperwork/information-collection renewal with no new duty, or a correction that changes nothing material;
- only mentions the company's topic without imposing anything.
Return exactly one decision per document number given — no more, no fewer.

Affected areas:
- aml-bsa: AML/BSA program, FinCEN, Travel Rule, SARs
- sanctions: OFAC screening and sanctions compliance
- consumer-payments: Reg E, remittances, prepaid, CFPB supervision, UDAAP
- crypto: Custodial wallet, stablecoins, CVC-specific rules
- privacy: Privacy, data security, open banking / 1033
- tax: Information reporting (1099-K, 1099-DA)
prompt:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps

- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

[2026-22809] Proposed Rule — Treasury Department; Financial Crimes Enforcement Network
Title: Threshold for the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Funds Transfers and Transmittals of Funds That Begin or End Outside the United States, and Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status; Withdrawal
Action: Proposed rule; withdrawal.
Abstract: FinCEN and the Board (collectively, the "Agencies") are withdrawing the joint notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published on October 27, 2020, that proposed modifying the threshold in the Agencies' rules implementing the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) requiring financial institutions to collect and retain information on certain funds transfers and transmittals of funds. The NPRM would have reduced this threshold from $3,000 to $250 for funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. FinCEN additionally proposed reducing from $3,000 to $250 the threshold in FinCEN's rule requiring financial institutions to transmit to other financial institutions in the payment chain information on funds transfers and transmittals of funds that begin or end outside the United States. The NPRM also would have clarified the meaning of "money" as used in the Agencies' rules to specify that the rules apply to domestic and cross-border transactions involving convertible virtual currency (CVC) and digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. The Agencies will not take further action on this NPRM.

Title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving MEXC Global
Action: Order.
Abstract: FinCEN is issuing notice of an order, pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Pub. L. 116- 283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81), finding that MEXC Global--including any of its subsidiaries, branches, and offices, as well as any successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States--is a financial institution operating outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance and prohibiting certain transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global.
Key passages from the full text (selected for this company):
- "CVC exchanger to a list of suspicious CVC trading platforms \22\--and, importantly, that, between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global facilitated the movement of USD 16.7 billion in funds connected to Russian illicit finance and other illicit activities, including sanctions evasion and cybercrime, posing a significant threat to the U.S. financial system. Indeed, within those transactions, FinCEN identified numerous instances in which MEXC Global processed transactions in violation of its own user agreement, including direct transactions between MEXC Global and sanctioned actors, some of whom were operating from MEXC Global's list of prohibited jurisdictions.\23\ --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \21\ MEXC Global has been the subject of regulatory scrutiny and has been found to be operating without a license in Seychelles, Hong Kong, and Japan. Document 2026-22962: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving MEXC Global

This action is effective December 10, 2026.

 
 
 Federal Register, Volume 91 Issue 216 (Tuesday, November 10, 2026) 
 
  
[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 216 (Tuesday, November 10, 2026)]
[Rules and Regulations]
[Pages 72420-72427]
From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [ www.gpo.gov ]
[FR Doc No: 2026-22962]


=======================================================================
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY

Financial Crimes Enforcement Network

31 CFR Part 1010


Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of 
Funds Involving MEXC Global

AGENCY: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Treasury.

ACTION: Order.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: FinCEN is issuing notice of an order, pursuant to section 
9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Pub. L. 116-
283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense 
Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81), finding that 
MEXC Global--including any of its subsidiaries, branches, and offices, 
as well as any successor entities, operating in any jurisdiction 
outside of the United States--is a financial institution operating 
outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in 
connection with Russian illicit finance and prohibiting certain 
transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global.

DATES: This action is effective December 10, 2026.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: FinCEN's Regulatory Support Section by 
submitting an inquiry at  www.fincen.gov/contact .

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

I. Summary of Order

    As set out in this order, MEXC Global has facilitated funds 
transfers by Russia-affiliated illicit actors and in connection with 
other Russia-associated illicit activities, including sanctions 
evasion, and activity facilitated by Russian darknet markets. It has 
also facilitated billions of dollars in transactions benefitting Iran 
and its proxies, financial facilitators of the Democratic People's 
Republic of Korea (DPRK), and other cybercrime actors. Accordingly, 
this order (1) sets forth FinCEN's determination that MEXC Global, a 
convertible virtual currency (CVC) exchanger, along with any 
subsidiaries, branches, and offices of MEXC Global, and any successor 
entities, operating in any jurisdiction outside of the United States 
(collectively, MEXC Global) \1\ is a financial institution operating 
outside of the United States of primary money laundering concern in 
connection with Russian illicit finance; and (2) prohibits certain 
transmittals of funds involving MEXC Global, by any covered financial 
institution.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \1\ This includes, but is not limited to, active and past MEXC 
affiliated entities MEXC Global Ltd/MX Global Ltd (Seychelles); MEXC 
Estonia O[Uuml] (Estonia); GIDA Technology AG (Switzerland); and MXC 
Global Ltd (United Kingdom); affiliated entities formerly 
incorporated in Singapore MEXC Global Foundation Ltd and MEXC 
Singapore Pte Ltd; and any successor entities.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

II. Background

A. Statutory Provisions

    Section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Pub. 
L. 116-283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense 
Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81) (section 
9714),\2\ provides, in relevant part, that, if the Secretary of the 
Treasury (Secretary) ``determines that reasonable grounds exist for 
concluding that one or more financial institutions operating outside of 
the United States . . . is of primary money laundering concern in 
connection with Russian illicit finance,'' the Secretary may, ``by 
order, regulation, or otherwise as permitted by law'': (1) require 
domestic financial institutions and domestic financial agencies to take 
one or more of the special measures described in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(b); 
\3\ or (2) prohibit, or impose conditions upon, certain transmittals of 
funds (as defined by the Secretary) by any domestic financial 
institution or domestic financial agency (collectively, covered 
financial institutions), if such transmittal of funds involves any such 
financial institution. The authority of the Secretary to administer 
both section 9714 and the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) has been delegated to 
FinCEN.\4\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \2\ Section 9714 (as amended) may be found in a note to 31 
U.S.C. 5318A.
    \3\ See infra note [4].
    \4\ Pursuant to Treasury Order 180-01, the authority of the 
Secretary of the Treasury (Secretary) to administer the BSA, 
including, but not limited to, 31 U.S.C. 5318A, has been delegated 
to the Director of FinCEN. Treasury Order 180-01 (Jan. 14, 2020). On 
August 11, 2022, and in accordance with Treasury Order 101-05 and 31 
U.S.C. 321(b), Treasury's Under Secretary for Terrorism & Financial 
Intelligence re-delegated to the Director of FinCEN the authority of 
the Secretary under section 9714.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Pursuant to section 9714, the Secretary may impose one or more of 
six special measures. First, the Secretary may impose any of the five 
special measures provided for in 31 U.S.C. 5318A(b), commonly known as 
section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act.\5\ Through special measures one 
through four, the Secretary may impose additional recordkeeping, 
information collection, and reporting requirements on covered financial 
institutions.\6\ Through special measure five, the Secretary, in 
consultation with the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the 
Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, may 
``prohibit, or impose conditions upon, the opening or maintaining in 
the United States of a correspondent account or payable-through 
account'' for or on behalf of a foreign banking institution, if such 
correspondent account or payable-through account involves the financial 
institution operating outside of the United States found to be of 
primary money laundering concern.\7\ In addition

[[Page 72421]]

to the special measures set out in 31 U.S.C. 5318A, section 9714 also 
provides that the Secretary may impose a special measure prohibiting, 
or imposing conditions upon, certain transmittals of funds.\8\

Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually
